claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes, which the cloud provider enforces independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides cloud-provider-side deletion protection.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides cloud-provider-side deletion protection.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (`protect` not set) and still refuse to delete because of provider-side deletion protection, or vice versa (protected in Pulumi but not protected by the cloud provider).

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section titled 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` resource option.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (a deletion-protection setting on the resource itself, separate from Pulumi's `protect`).
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (a deletion-protection setting on the resource itself, separate from Pulumi's `protect`).

Pulumi's `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi only, while resource-level deletion protection is enforced by the provider or cloud API; the two layers are complementary rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' on the destroy-failures troubleshooting page (/docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/#deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself) exists and explains how to tell Pulumi `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails on a protected resource, the error message names the resource URN and mentions `protect`.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ explains how to remove the `protect` resource option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, and the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection` is enforced by the cloud API, which rejects the delete call independent of Pulumi.
AWS EC2 `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the cloud API, which rejects the delete call independent of Pulumi.
An Azure Resource Manager management lock causes the cloud API to reject the delete call independent of Pulumi.
Cloud-API-enforced deletion protection errors come back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked` (Azure management lock).
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the Pulumi program currently says.
Setting a deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program is not enough on its own for `pulumi destroy` to succeed; the change must first be applied.

To remove provider-enforced or cloud-API-enforced deletion protection, set the attribute to `false` in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches both the live resource and Pulumi's state, then run `pulumi destroy`.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality, and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`; a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist in the Pulumi Azure Native provider for creating management locks.
Azure Resource Manager enforces management locks; a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
